rationale: The candidate reads as one dominant mass, but the visible four-view set shows a compact, slightly faceted block with a weakly articulated upper carve rather than a strong neighborhood-living street building. The blue access edge is not met with a clearly public ground threshold: the open/void logic is too shallow and reads more like a clipped side notch than a usable court, entry seam, or terrace. Across views, the form is coherent enough to avoid a fragmentation penalty, but it is still close to a generic extruded mass with minor surface/edge modulation. The stepped/angled section has some resonance with the prism reference, yet the candidate lacks the stronger podium/void hierarchy and public ground response seen in the better references. Programmatically, it can plausibly hold mixed-use neighborhood living only weakly; the section does not yet advertise an active lower public zone or a convincing program-led void, so it fails the hard pass.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stacked massing over a clear podium/void relation; useful as a precedent for legible hierarchy and a more decisive upper-vs-ground split.
